newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Socialist supporters urge counter-rallies.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Socialist supporters urge counter-rallies.

text.p: Bulgaria's ruling Socialists on Tuesday threatened a tougher response to opposition rallies, saying provincial party organisations had urged the party leadership to organise counter-rallies.

"They insist that we must have a tougher approach against the pressure of the opposition. Our local organisations also want to organise counter-rallies to respond to the opposition protest rallies," Vassil Karinov, a member of the party executive bureau, told reporters as daily protests entered their third week.
Counter-rallies by supporters of neighbouring Serbia's Socialist President Slobodan Milosevic in Belgrade on December 24 led to violent clashes between demonstrators and riot police.

Karinov said the Bulgarian Socialist Party was sticking to its insistence on forming a new government until general elections at the end of the year, and planned to introduce emergency economic measures in the next few weeks, including rescheduling the country's huge domestic debt.
"We think that immediate elections for Bulgaria are not the best alternative for the country because we need a tough restrictive regime even before a currency board system is introduced," he said.

The main opposition Union of Democratic Forces, which wants elections as soon as possible, also presented an economic programme, saying that if elections were held in March, a currency board fixed exchange rate regime could be introduced as early as May.
